<subject>Re: Greenfields' Petition To Be Released From QF Contracts</subject>
<body>
Rajiv Menon -

My understanding is that Kapoor does not have the legal authority (and the filing never clarifies) to suspend performance under the Power Purchase Agreement (he likely lacks the political backing for this as well).

However, the Agricultural Producers Association could support this in its filing as a way to help advance the QF issue.

Regards,  
Arjun Patel


Ravi Kumar  
Sent by: Ravi Kumar  
04/12/2024 09:15 AM  

To: Rajiv Menon/Corp/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Sunita Reddy/Corp/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Meera Shah/HQ/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Anil Desai/Corp/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Nisha Iyer/NA/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Arjun Patel/NA/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Vikram Singh/NA/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Prakash Rao/PDX/AgriIndia@AGRIND, Kavita Joshi/NA/AgriIndia@AGRIND  
Subject: Greenfields' Petition To Be Released From QF Contracts

FYI. Any thoughts Rajiv & team? Is release from contracts considered an "increase supply" option? My concern is that if QFs get released, the state government might respond with strict regulations, executive orders, or legislation to ensure power from the QF facilities remains within the state.

Best regards,  
Ravi

Dear Colleagues,

In view of the potential power shortages in the region today and in the coming days, Greenfields Energy requests your organization’s intervention to support the attached emergency filing at the regulatory commission. Please forward this email to your legal department and ask them to contact either our legal counsel, Meera Kapoor (022-496-3456), our General Counsel, Ramesh Singh (1800-555-7890, ext. 101), or me directly at (1800-555-7890, ext. 207). Any assistance would be greatly appreciated.

Sincerely,  
Rohit Sharma
